posts.title: Nio reaches 500 swap stations in Guangdong, with over 17 million swaps completed
posts.summary:
Guangdong accounts for about 13% of Nio's cumulative battery swaps in China.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio has reached a milestone of 500 battery swap stations in Guangdong, a key economic region that accounts for 13% of the company's total cumulative battery swaps in China.
The company reported a 76.3% year-on-year sales increase in Guangdong during the first eight months of 2026, significantly outpacing its national delivery growth rate of 57.92% for the same period.

Nio has shifted its regional strategy from achieving basic county-level coverage to increasing station density, having already successfully covered all 122 county-level administrative areas in the province by 2025.

The infrastructure expansion includes 101 highway-based swap stations in Guangdong, which have facilitated over 3 million swaps and support critical transit routes like the Pearl River Delta Ring Expressway.

posts.title: Energy Dome and its carbon dioxide batteries
posts.summary: There’s a growing need for long-duration storage to meet energy demand and balance out renewables on the grid. Energy Dome uses compressed carbon dioxide gas in its massive grid batteries, which can deliver power for up to 24 hours.  As the world races to meet growing electricity demand, solar and onshore wind power have become…
bullets: Energy Dome uses compressed carbon dioxide in a closed-loop system to provide long-duration energy storage, offering a scalable alternative to lithium-ion for grid balancing.
The system stores energy by compressing CO2 into a liquid state and releases it through a turbine to generate electricity when needed, with a capacity of up to 24 hours.
Following the launch of its first commercial plant in Sardinia in 2025, the company is planning 30 gigawatt-hours of projects across five continents.

posts.title: Closing The Visibility Gap
posts.summary:
More measurements don’t eliminate blind spots when each view captures only part of the device.
The post Closing The Visibility Gap appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: More measurements don’t eliminate blind spots when each view captures only part of the device.

Key Takeaways:
Advanced chips now come with an extraordinary amount of evidence about them.

They’re modeled before they exist, measured during fabrication, inspected during assembly, electrically tested at the wafer and package levels, characterized under thermal and power loads, and increasingly monitored...
In some ways, engineers can see more of a device than ever before.
The problem is that each of those views is partial.
